title: The proper projection formula on the rational localizing categories
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ and let $p:X\to Y$ be proper. For
$A\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ and $B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$ the projection
formula map

$$
(Rp_*A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\longrightarrow Rp_*(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*B)
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Use the standing separated finite-type scheme setting, and the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings, throughout; no replacement by the category of discrete rational sheaves is made. These schemes are qcqs. For $T=X,Y$, the rational cases of the finite-Tor comparison give $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)=\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ and equality of their localizing closures. Thus all the subsequent localizing restriction and determination statements, formulated using $\Dctf$, apply to precisely the categories in this statement.

source.place: first paragraph: interpretation of the rational localizing categories

proof.text: Apply the inverse-image restriction with $g=p$ and the proper-image restriction with $p$ as in the statement. The latter explicitly asserts that its hypotheses hold for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$; it is not being applied only conditionally. Using Step 1, both functors are exact and preserve all small direct sums on the displayed localizing categories. Tensor closure, applied on both $X$ and $Y$, gives $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*B\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ and $(Rp_*A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$. Applying $Rp_*$ to the former gives the other term in the target localizing category.

source.place: first paragraph: restrictions and both terms of the map

proof.text:
Derived tensor is exact in each variable by the ringed-topos tensor statement. It preserves direct sums in each variable: the closed structure supplies $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}-\dashv\RHom(C,-)$, and for every $N$ the adjunction identifies
$\Hom(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}\bigoplus_i M_i,N)$ with $\Hom(\bigoplus_i M_i,\RHom(C,N))=\prod_i\Hom(M_i,\RHom(C,N))=\prod_i\Hom(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}M_i,N)$.
These identifications are the coproduct universal property. Symmetry gives the other variable. Since the localizing subcategories are full and their coproducts are the ambient coproducts, these properties restrict to them. Together with Step 2 this proves that both sides of the projection map, with either input fixed, are exact functors preserving direct sums.

source.place: first paragraph and second paragraph: tensor exactness and direct sums

proof.text:
The module pullback is the ringed-topos pullback, and the Cartesian coefficient isomorphism identifies it with exact inverse image, so $Lp^*=p^*$. Put $L=p^*$, $R=Rp_*$, and let $\varepsilon:LR\to1$ be the derived counit. The canonical unbounded projection map $\pi_{A,B}$ is the adjoint transpose of
$L(RA\otimes^{\mathbf L}B)\xrightarrow{\mu}LRA\otimes^{\mathbf L}LB\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_A\otimes1}A\otimes^{\mathbf L}LB$.
The ringed projection-mate statement supplies this map for arbitrary unbounded inputs, natural in both inputs, and the shift compatibility of $\mu$. Give the exact functor $L$ its shift isomorphisms $e_L$ and give $R$ the shift structure $e_R$ of clause (iii) of the abstract adjunction-shift lemma, so that unit and counit commute with the shifts; in particular $\varepsilon_{A[1]}=\varepsilon_A[1]\circ e_{L,RA}\circ L(e_{R,A})$. By the triangulated-right-adjoint statement, $R$ with $e_R$ is exact; these are the shift structures of $Rp_*$ used in Steps 6 and 7, and the restriction of Step 2 is exact for them, being the restriction of this exact functor to full triangulated subcategories. In the variable $A$: substitute the counit formula in the displayed transpose at $(A[1],B)$ and use the shift compatibility of $\mu$; after the tensor shift identifications, the transpose at $(A[1],B)$ is exactly the shift of the transpose at $(A,B)$. In the variable $B$: at $(A,B[1])$ the counit factor is unchanged, and the shift compatibility of $\mu$ and of the tensor give the same conclusion. Since unit and counit commute with $e_L,e_R$, the adjunction bijection commutes with shifts and gives the corresponding equalities $s_G\pi_{-[1]}=\pi_{-}[1]s_F$ for $\pi$ in each variable. Naturality and these shift identities make the components on every distinguished triangle a morphism of triangles, including the connecting square, in either variable. Thus the determination lemma will apply to the actual canonical map, with exact structures for which both functors are exact.

source.place: first paragraph: canonical map and exact natural transformations; Stacks 0B56, 07A4, 07A6 and 0A8D

proof.text: If $A\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and $B\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, clause (3) of the rational proper-base-change theorem says precisely that this canonical proper projection formula map is an isomorphism. Its standing-scheme, properness, and rational-coefficient hypotheses hold here.

source.place: second paragraph: bounded constructible base case

proof.text: Fix $B\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, so in particular $B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$. By Steps 2--4 the functors $A\mapsto (Rp_*A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}B$ and $A\mapsto Rp_*(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*B)$ have common codomain $\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$, are exact and preserve direct sums, and $\pi_{-,B}$ is a natural transformation of exact functors. Step 5 gives invertibility on $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. The determination lemma, using the equalities of Step 1, gives invertibility for every $A\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ and this bounded $B$.

source.place: second paragraph: first fix B bounded and extend in A

proof.text: Now fix any $A\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$. By Steps 2--4 both functors of $B$ are exact and preserve direct sums, with the same target localizing category, and $\pi_{A,-}$ is a natural transformation of exact functors. By Step 6 it is an isomorphism for every bounded constructible $B$. Apply the determination lemma with source scheme $Y$ and target scheme $Y$, and the equalities of Step 1, to obtain invertibility for all $B\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$. This is the required isomorphism in the full target localizing category.

source.place: second paragraph: fix A arbitrary and extend in B
